question_text:
### Production Incident Scenario:
Production Incident #06: An executive revenue dashboard reported an overnight 200% discrepancy in Customer Lifetime Value (LTV) and Month-over-Month retention in Advanced SQL Querying & Relational Joins. Audit logs show data pipeline inaccuracies stemming from 'Window Functions (ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK, NTILE)'.

### Engineering Challenge:
What is the correct analytical SQL and data modeling approach to ensure accurate metric aggregation for 'Window Functions (ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK, NTILE)'?

options.text: Enforce distinct user-level keys in dimensional joins, isolate fan-out via CTE pre-aggregations, and utilize window framing (ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW).
Execute a CROSS JOIN between customer tables and raw event logs without deduplication.
Hardcode arbitrary multiplier factors into the reporting query to offset the calculated inflation.
Suppress all rows with duplicate dates by applying SELECT DISTINCT * across the entire warehouse.

answer_explanation: Metric distortion in Advanced SQL Querying & Relational Joins typically arises from accidental Cartesian joins or improper window framing that multi-counts transactions when dimensional tables have multiple active rows. Pre-aggregating at the user/date grain before joining eliminates fan-out.
reference_solution: Recommended Remediation: Option A. Rationale: Metric distortion in Advanced SQL Querying & Relational Joins typically arises from accidental Cartesian joins or improper window framing that multi-counts transactions when dimensional tables have multiple active rows. Pre-aggregating at the user/date grain before joining eliminates fan-out.
